svg.title: Accuracy as the same Hamiltonian grows: six instance ladders
svg.desc: J1-J2 square, J2 = 0.5, periodic: 112 energies at sizes 16, 36, 40, 64, 100, 144, 196, 256, 324, 400; Heisenberg square, periodic: 43 energies at sizes 16, 36, 40, 50, 64, 100, 144, 196, 256, 324, 400, 484, 576, 676, 784, 900, 1024, 1296, 1600, 1936, 2304, 2704, 3136, 3600, 4096, 5184, 6400, 7744, 9216; Heisenberg triangular, periodic: 20 energies at sizes 16, 36, 48, 108, 144; Heisenberg kagome, periodic: 10 energies at sizes 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48, 192; Heisenberg pyrochlore, periodic: 21 energies at sizes 32, 108, 128, 256, 432, 1024; Hubbard U = 8, n = 0.875, periodic: 58 energies at sizes 32, 64, 224, 256, 288
svg.text: Accuracy as the same Hamiltonian grows
Six families of instances that differ only in size. Distance is from the exact energy where one exists (sizes in grey), otherwise
from the standing record (sizes in orange), whose holder then sits in the band under the axis. One line per method family,
through its best energy at each size; a family present at one size only is a lone mark.
J1-J2 square, J2 = 0.5, periodic (119 energies, 10 sizes)
Hubbard U = 8, n = 0.875, periodic (64 energies, 5 sizes)
Sizes are numbers of sites. A family's line joins its lowest distance at each size, whichever paper set it, so a line is a family's reach rather
than one calculation. Where the reference is the record, the distances say how far behind the others are and nothing about the record itself.
